figures.recommended_generation_prompt: Create a precise, photorealistic engineering teaching illustration as a wide landscape diptych, approximately 3.5:1. Two equal side-by-side panels show the SAME single-bay radial (tainter) spillway gate in vertical side cutaway, viewed from the same downstream-facing side angle. Clean off-white background, realistic restrained concrete and galvanized steel, crisp readable surfaces, soft daylight, no dramatic flood or cinematic effects. Upstream is LEFT, downstream is RIGHT. Clearly show the curved steel gate skin, radial support arms leading to a downstream trunnion on a concrete pier, concrete sill and horizontal channel floor. The gate is partly open, leaving a visible vertical clearance between its bottom edge and the sill. Upper-left upstream reservoir water level is identical in both panels. LEFT PANEL: low downstream water and a visibly free under-gate jet, the jet and the vertical gate clearance are easy to distinguish. RIGHT PANEL: raised downstream tailwater submerges the outlet region, with no free jet into air. Keep gate geometry, opening, floor elevation and viewpoint identical; only downstream water level changes. Use transparent cutaway water near the gate so the opening remains visible, and subtle natural flow texture, not physically claimed CFD streamlines. Leave a narrow clean margin above and beside the water surfaces for later vector annotations. The image is conceptual teaching rendering, not an existing real engineering site. NO text, NO labels, NO letters, NO numbers, NO dimensions, NO equations, NO legend, NO logo, NO watermark, NO invented instruments. Do not depict a vertically sliding flat sluice gate. Ensure mechanical parts connect plausibly. The result must remain legible when printed at 14.6 cm wide.
